companies.name: Aylo (formerly MindGeek)
companies.description: Operator of major adult-content platforms including Pornhub, YouPorn, and RedTube, using third-party identity verification (Yoti) for content uploaders and various age-assurance methods for viewers depending on jurisdiction.
companies.notes: Not a dedicated identity-verification vendor; included because it retained performers' identity documents and Social Security numbers collected through its verification process.

companies.name: Serasa Experian (Brazil)
companies.description: Brazilian subsidiary of global credit bureau Experian, providing credit scoring, identity verification, and KYC data products to Brazilian businesses.
companies.notes: Experian disputes that its own systems were breached, but the leaked dataset closely resembled Serasa data categories and was widely attributed to the company in Brazilian reporting and litigation.

companies.name: Buró de Crédito (Mexico)
companies.description: Mexico's principal credit-reporting bureau, used by banks and lenders for identity verification and creditworthiness checks nationwide.
companies.notes: Mexico's banking regulator CNBV was notified of a possible data exposure in 2022-2023; full scope and attribution remained publicly unconfirmed at initial reporting.

companies.name: EguWallet
companies.description: eIDAS 2.0-certified European Digital Identity Wallet developed by IT Eguilde SRL, allowing citizens to store and present ID cards, driving licences, diplomas, and qualified signatures from a mobile device.
companies.notes: No confirmed public breach identified as of research date.

companies.name: Persona (ONYX government platform)
companies.description: Persona's separate FedRAMP-authorized government platform offering facial recognition, watchlist screening, and Suspicious Activity Report filing capabilities.
companies.notes: Separate product line from Persona's mainstream consumer identity-verification service.

companies.name: Total Wireless (Verizon)
companies.description: US prepaid wireless carrier owned by Verizon that used Veriff to verify customer identity documents for a promotional offer.
companies.notes: Customer IDs submitted via vendor Veriff were exposed in a vendor-system breach.

companies.name: Police National Legal Database (PNLD)
companies.description: UK legal lookup and reference service used by police forces and criminal-justice agencies.
companies.notes: Included because it stored and exposed identity/contact information of officers, staff, and criminal-justice professionals.

companies.name: FranceConnect+
companies.description: France's official digital-identity single sign-on system for public and private online services.
companies.notes: No confirmed public breach identified; distinct from France Titres/ANTS.

companies.name: SPID (Sistema Pubblico di Identità Digitale, Italy)
companies.description: Italy's public digital-identity system used by over 30 million citizens to access public and private online services.
companies.notes: No confirmed public breach identified as of research date.

companies.name: DNIe / Cl@ve (Spain)
companies.description: Spain's national electronic identity card and associated Cl@ve digital-identity authentication system.
companies.notes: No confirmed public breach identified as of research date.

companies.name: eID-Funktion / Personalausweis (Germany)
companies.description: Germany's electronic ID-card identity function enabling online authentication to government and private services.
companies.notes: No confirmed public breach identified as of research date.

companies.name: Android Developer Verification (Google)
companies.description: Google's identity-verification program for Android app developers, with enforcement beginning September 30, 2026 in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand.
companies.notes: No confirmed public breach identified as of research date.

companies.name: Bitnob
companies.description: Nigeria-headquartered cryptocurrency and Bitcoin-focused fintech platform requiring KYC identity verification for customer onboarding.
companies.notes: KYC documents were exposed via misconfigured cloud storage.

companies.name: Betty Gaming (Betty.ca)
companies.description: Ontario-licensed online casino and sports-betting operator required to verify player age and identity.
companies.notes: Age-verification control failure, not an external data breach.

companies.name: Ghana National Identification Authority (Ghana Card)
companies.description: Ghana's national identity authority issuing biometric Ghana Cards and operating the national identity register.
companies.notes: No confirmed public breach identified as of research date.

companies.name: Uganda National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA)
companies.description: Uganda's authority responsible for the national identification register and biometric national IDs.
companies.notes: No confirmed public breach identified as of research date.

companies.name: Huduma Namba / NIIMS (Kenya)
companies.description: Kenya's biometric-linked National Integrated Identity Management System for government services.
companies.notes: No confirmed public breach identified; programme has faced privacy and legal scrutiny.

companies.name: EU Age Verification App (EUDI prototype)
companies.description: European Commission prototype age-verification application built on EUDI Wallet technology.
companies.notes: Security bypass reported; no identity-document data exposure reported.

breaches.title: Aylo (Pornhub) FTC Settlement Over Unsecured Performer ID Data
breaches.summary: FTC and Utah found Aylo retained performer identity data without encryption, access restrictions, or a firewall.
breaches.details: Regulators alleged Aylo retained performer Social Security numbers, addresses, birthdates, and identity information indefinitely after verification. The settlement required safeguards, verification improvements, and legacy-content remediation. This is a regulatory finding of inadequate identity-data security, not a confirmed external hack.

breaches.title: Serasa Experian Brazil Data Exposure (223 Million Records)
breaches.summary: A dataset of over 223 million Brazilian personal records appeared for sale, with data categories closely resembling Serasa Experian products.
breaches.details: The dataset included CPF identifiers, names, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers, emails, salary ranges and credit scores. Experian investigated but disputed that its systems were compromised; this disputed attribution is explicitly recorded.

breaches.title: Buró de Crédito Mexico Data Exposure
breaches.summary: Mexico's banking regulator knew of a possible Buró de Crédito exposure after data was advertised for sale on Telegram.
breaches.details: The CNBV confirmed awareness of the potential incident in late 2022. Scope and confirmed attribution remained publicly unconfirmed in initial reporting.

breaches.title: Persona ONYX Government Dashboard Source-Code Exposure
breaches.summary: Researchers found 2,456 files of source code from Persona's FedRAMP-authorized government dashboard publicly exposed.
breaches.details: The exposed ONYX code reportedly revealed watchlist screening, PEP checks, biometric retention settings, and direct suspicious-activity-report functionality. No confirmed individual-record theft was reported.

breaches.title: Veriff Breach Exposes Total Wireless Customer IDs
breaches.summary: A Veriff-system breach exposed government ID images and personal details for 8,583 Total Wireless customers.
breaches.details: Total Wireless said the unauthorized party accessed data in vendor Veriff's systems, including government ID images submitted for a promotional verification process.

breaches.title: Police National Legal Database (PNLD) Data Theft
breaches.summary: The UK Police National Legal Database confirmed theft and dark-web publication of officer and staff contact information.
breaches.details: The information included names, organisations and work email addresses of police officers, staff and criminal justice professionals. PNLD said no password compromise was identified.

breaches.title: Bitnob KYC Document Exposure via Misconfigured AWS Bucket
breaches.summary: A public AWS bucket exposed more than 250,000 KYC documents from Nigerian crypto platform Bitnob.
breaches.details: The exposed onboarding documents included government IDs, passports and driver's licenses. The bucket was secured after disclosure.

breaches.title: Betty Gaming Fined Over Age-Verification Control Failures
breaches.summary: Ontario's gambling regulator fined Betty Gaming after age-verification failures allowed minors to create and fund gambling accounts.
breaches.details: The self-reported defect allowed 23 underage users to create accounts and 9 to deposit and wager. This is a regulatory control failure, not a document-data breach.

breaches.title: EU Age Verification App Security Bypass
breaches.summary: Researchers showed the European Commission's prototype age-verification app could be bypassed within minutes.
breaches.details: The application stored an encrypted PIN locally but did not cryptographically bind it to the identity vault. No identity-document data exposure was reported.

source_audit.purpose: Consolidated source audit metadata from batches 3-6.

source_audit.review_policy: All discoveries are candidates requiring human review before publication.
